about: WorldScrawl prompts. Edit them in the map window: Tools > Prompt Editor. {{name}} is filled in by the game.

groups.title: Player intent
groups.flow: Runs on every message the player sends, before the narrator replies. Step 1: one multiple-choice question asks what the player is doing. The game builds the list of choices from the option pieces: one line per exit and per known place, plus 'breaking through', 'look', 'open/close a door' or 'a door not on the map' only when the message uses one of those kinds of words. The answer decides what happens next: an exit or place moves the party; breaking through goes to 'Breaking through'; look goes to 'Looking'; opening or closing a door goes to 'Doors'; a door not on the map tells the narrator to open it if it fits (which can lead to 'New room behind a door'); otherwise the party stays. Step 2 (only if the answer can't be read and no place name matches): a yes/no question asks whether the player is trying to travel at all. Yes means 'somewhere unlisted', no means they stay. Whatever happened is then handed to 'Narration'.

groups.title: Breaking through
groups.flow: Runs when Player intent decides the player is breaking a new opening (a hole in a wall, floor or window). It asks a chain of small questions, one at a time, all with the same system prompt. Each answer is checked by the game and that one question is asked again once if the answer doesn't fit. Step 1: where does it lead (a nearby place or somewhere new). Step 2: what the opening is called from this side. Steps 3 and 4 (only for somewhere new): a name and a one-sentence description for the new room. If any step fails, nothing is changed and the narrator is told nothing gave way. Otherwise the game makes the opening, saves it on the player's message, then Step 5 asks whether the player stays on this side; anything but a clear 'yes' moves the party through. The result is handed to 'Narration'.

groups.title: Looking
groups.flow: Runs when Player intent decides the player is looking or listening. 'Look around' needs no question. Step 1: what are they looking at: around in general, one of the exits, or out of a window (only offered if a window is mentioned or the room has a view). Step 2 depends on the pick: for a closed door, ask whether they listen, peek, open it, or just look at it; for a window with no view set yet, ask which nearby place can be seen (the answer is saved so it's the same next time). The game then works out what can be seen or heard and hands it to 'Narration'.

groups.title: Doors
groups.flow: Runs when Player intent decides the player opens or closes a door. If only one door fits, no question is asked. Step 1 (only with several doors): which door. The game fills {{verb}} with "open" or "close". The game then opens or closes it (or notes it is stuck), saves that on the player's message, and hands it to 'Narration'.

groups.title: Narration
groups.flow: Not a separate model call: this is the block of world facts the game adds to the narrator's own prompt every turn, so the story matches the map. It is put together in order: Step 1 the first line; then the game's own facts (place, exits, what can be seen, time, weather); Step 2 one 'what just happened' line chosen from the result of Player intent, Breaking through, Looking or Doors (a move, a journey, breaking through, a door, a door not on the map, looking around, and so on); Step 3 things passed on the way (after a move); Step 4 a nudge to mention the exits; Step 5 the last line with the rules. Alongside it: the arrival reminder goes after the latest message on move turns, and when map tools are off the two 'how to flag' hints tell the narrator to end a reply with [ws_flag: …] or [ws_wait: …] tags, which start 'Map changes', 'New room behind a door' or a wait.

groups.title: Map changes
groups.flow: Runs when a message is flagged as changing the map: the flag button, the narrator's ws_flag tool or [ws_flag: …] tag, or /ws-change. Step 1: given the story and an outline of the nearby map, the model answers in JSON which places changed. If none, it stops. Step 2: the game sends just those places (plus neighbours and other mentions, via the pieces) and the list of map edits the editor can make; the model answers with JSON edits, or says it can't express it, or that nothing changed. The game test-applies the edits; if they don't fit the map, Step 2 is asked once more with the retry piece explaining the error. The result becomes a review card (or is kept at once if 'keep automatically' is on).

groups.title: New room behind a door
groups.flow: Runs when the narrator opens a door that isn't on the map yet and flags it as a discovery (from the 'door not on the map' narration). Step 1: the model gets the region and area notes, the current room, its exits, nearby rooms and the story, and answers in JSON with the new room and the door pair. The game turns that into the same 'create place' edit the editor uses and test-applies it; if it doesn't fit, Step 1 is asked once more with the retry piece. The room is added at once, as if it had always been there, unless 'review discoveries' is on.

groups.title: Expand with AI
groups.flow: Runs when you press 'Expand with AI' under a description or notes box in the map editor. Step 1: one call with the place's region, area and connected places, which box it is (the field pieces), and your draft if the box already has text. The reply is put into the box for you to keep or change; nothing is saved until you save the form.

placeholders.address: the address of the room behind the door
placeholders.area: the address of the area being changed
placeholders.areas: the area notes that apply, for context
placeholders.arrival: what the party sees on arrival (the new room's description)
placeholders.compass: the compass directions to choose from, e.g. "north, south, east, west, up, down, …"
placeholders.context: what is already around the place (its region, area and neighbours), or empty
placeholders.cut_short: empty, or " (the trip was cut short there)" when the trip stopped early (the Narration piece)
placeholders.description: the description of the room the prompt is about
placeholders.destination: where the new opening leads, as already worked out in the step before
placeholders.direction: the exit or direction, e.g. "north", "up" or "through the trapdoor"
placeholders.door: the door being used, e.g. "the north door"
placeholders.draft: your draft text for the field, or empty (the Expand with AI piece)
placeholders.edit_types: the list of map edit types the model may use (made by the game)
placeholders.end: where the story text to look at ends
placeholders.error: what was wrong with the last answer
placeholders.exits: the list of exits from the current room, one per line, or "- (none)" when there are none
placeholders.field: which text to write: the description or the notes (the Expand with AI pieces)
placeholders.how_to_flag: how the narrator should flag a new door: the tools version or the [ws_flag] tag version (the Narration pieces)
placeholders.kind: what kind of place it is: "region", "area" or "room"
placeholders.label: the name of a place the player already knows about
placeholders.mentions: other world text that names a changed place (from the Map changes piece), or empty
placeholders.name: the name of the place (new or being changed)
placeholders.near: the places near the new room
placeholders.neighbors: the places one step beyond the change (from the Map changes piece), or empty
placeholders.new_number: the number of the "somewhere new" option in the list
placeholders.new_place: the answer word that means "somewhere new"
placeholders.note: the narrator's note naming the door
placeholders.option: the short answer word for this choice, e.g. "look" or "stay"
placeholders.option_lines: the list of possible answers, one per line, each with what it means (built from the Player intent pieces)
placeholders.options: the possible answers, as a numbered list or a comma-separated list
placeholders.outline: an outline of the rooms and exits in the area
placeholders.party: who is travelling: the "Who moves" setting, e.g. your persona name, or your persona and the character
placeholders.place: the name of the room the party is in now
placeholders.places: the nearby places, as a numbered list with a short summary of each
placeholders.range: which rooms the patch may touch
placeholders.retry: empty, or a note that the last answer was rejected and why (the retry piece)
placeholders.rooms: the rooms that may be changed, with their current text
placeholders.said: what the player just wrote (their latest message)
placeholders.start: where the story text to look at starts
placeholders.steps: what happened on the way, step by step, joined with "Then:"
placeholders.story: the part of the story that changed the map
placeholders.to: the room the party arrived in
placeholders.used: directions this room already has exits in, or "none"
placeholders.verb: the door action: "open" or "close" in the door question; "opens" or "closes" in the narration line
placeholders.via: the rooms passed through on the way, comma separated
placeholders.what: what change was flagged, in the narrator's words
placeholders.where: where the party is now, for the narrator
placeholders.why: why the door would not move (e.g. it is locked)

prompts.title: Map changes: the patch (system prompt)
prompts.description: Step 2 of 2: the system prompt for writing the edits. {{edit_types}} is the editor's list of edits, made by the game. Second call: writes the map change. {{edit_types}} is the list of map edits the game supports; it is made from the code and cannot be edited here.
prompts.locked: The game reads the JSON edits in this exact format.
prompts.text:
You turn a lasting change in a story into a map patch. Reply with JSON only: {"ops": [...]}.
ADDR is a room's full address copied exactly from the map, e.g. "riverton:drowned_rat/common_room". AREA is a region id ("riverton") or subregion id ("riverton:drowned_rat"). Never invent addresses or ids: renaming a place changes its display name only, its address stays the same.
Allowed ops (exactly what the map editor can do):
{{edit_types}}
Example, a whole inn turned into a palace: {"ops":[{"op":"update_area","area":"riverton:drowned_rat","name":"The Golden Palace"},{"op":"set_description","loc":"riverton:drowned_rat/common_room","text":"A gilded throne hall; an old brass rail shows under the gold leaf."},{"op":"append_notes","area":"riverton:drowned_rat","text":"Formerly the Drowned Rat inn; transmogrified into a palace by magic."},{"op":"set_description","loc":"riverton:drowned_rat/courtyard","text":"..."}]}
Any op may add "lasts":"3d" (or "12h") if the change is temporary. Use as few ops as possible. Descriptions are present tense, 1-3 sentences, about the place, not the characters.
DESCRIPTION RULE: a description says only what the place IS now. Visible physical traces of the past are fine, because they are there now ("scorch marks blacken the beams", "an old brass rail shows under the gold leaf"). Never narrate the change itself: no "has been replaced by", "was transformed", "was once", "now". History goes in notes instead: a short append_notes on the place's area, e.g. {"op":"append_notes","area":"riverton:drowned_rat","text":"Formerly the Drowned Rat inn; transmogrified into a palace by magic."}. Exception: a temporary change with "lasts" (smoke, a fresh fire) may mention the event.
People and creatures mentioned in a room's description or notes are part of the room: if the story permanently changed one (hurt, killed, transformed, left, moved in), rewrite that part, following the description rule.
Exit names (the "direction", e.g. "grate", "narrow door") are hand-written: never rename them. A door's open/locked/blocked state and removing an exit apply to both sides; hidden, sight and text are per side. Only change what the story clearly changed. If nothing lasting changed, reply {"ops": []}.
If the story changed the map in a way none of these ops can express, do not force a wrong op: reply {"cant": "one short sentence saying what can't be shown on the map"}.
